external_basis.source: external Latin source-marker controls only; Voynich excluded from basis estimation
external_basis.weighting: one centroid per external class, equal class weight

decision.H59C_1: NOT SUPPORTED AS SUFFICIENT — external medieval entry rank-2 geometry explains about 65% of Voynich transition energy, not all of it
decision.H59C_2: SUPPORTED — a substantial shared medieval-entry component coexists with a stable Voynich-specific orthogonal component
decision.H59C_3: PARTIAL WARNING ONLY — external basis is sensitive to which small control class is omitted, but the orthogonal remainder never collapses and ranges ~0.58-0.99 in norm

interpretation: About two thirds of the squared magnitude of the Voynich paragraph-entry transition lies in a low-rank direction learned entirely from explicit medieval Latin entry markers. This is strong evidence that part of the phenomenon is a generic medieval document-entry/register effect rather than Voynich-unique machinery. However, the component orthogonal to that Latin basis remains positive across all five major Voynich sections H/B/P/S/T, with page-bootstrap 95% intervals above zero. The residual specialization is weakest in Biological and Stars and strongest in Herbal, Pharmaceutical and Text-only. This supports a shared entry grammar plus Voynich-specific specialization model.
cautions: External source-marker corpus remains small and heterogeneous.
Rank=2 is a development choice motivated by the external singular spectrum, not an externally validated dimensionality.
Generic feature coordinates are structural analogues across scripts, not semantic homologues.
A stable Voynich-specific structural component is not evidence of plaintext, cipher, or meaning.
next: Phase60 should characterize the Latin-orthogonal Voynich transition mechanistically: identify which audited structural features carry it, test whether it is driven by first-line token architecture/paragraph-start markers, and compare against formal/cipher generators.
